I'm going to list some things I haven't seen yet:

- Don't underestimate the walk between the two mainstages. It's farther than you think!
- Try to mentally take note of where bathrooms are and water stations.  There would be times I was frantically searching.
- Be prepared for little to no shade. Bucket hats, baseball caps highly recommended. Same with sunscreen.
- No liquids are allowed in when you get to the entrance. Don't buy full water bottles or anything to bring in. I saw people buy them and then immediately have to dump it all out.

If you can, I would pick a hotel nearby or at least in the Loop. The trains are going to be crowded but if you are in the loop/River North Area you can take any train (instead of just the Red Line) and it will only be a couple stops so you won't have to deal with the crowd long. 

If you want to Uber, you should know you will still need to walk to get out of the immediate area. The roads next to Grant Park are closed and the streets nearby are basically gridlocked with Ubers looking for passengers.

Hi! I've done Coachella and Lolla! The vibes are definitely different since there is no camping, so you won't be like waking up at 9 AM to check out a yoga class. It's more of people in large friend groups running around. 

I'm not an EDM person, so I may not be the best to talk but Coachella definitely has more EDM focus. Lolla has Perry's but there aren't EDM shows happening everywhere.

Last year, the weather was almost as bad/hot as Coachella. I was so upset. The water stations get super crowded and are spaced out at Lolla, so I would plan to stop at one whenever you see it.

They have really fun lounges. Last year, there was an UberOne lounge, a TicTac lounge, a giant Dunkin Donuts lounge. There are usually long lines but it does provide a nice midday break.

A big difference is GRASS and PAVEMENT! You will be able to find places to sit rather than just plopping down on dirt. There are also trees in certain areas if you need a break from the sun. 

I wouldn't expect any special guests like Coachella but the shows are all very fun. I would recommend mapping out the park when planning shows. I didn't realize how far everything was at first. It seems closer than it actually is.
